new.question: A sanitary sewer is surcharging and sewage is overflowing from a manhole onto a street. What should the operator do first?
options: Flush the overflow into the nearest storm drain to clear the street
Protect the public by restricting access, notify the supervisor and start the spill response procedure
Wait for the level to fall on its own before telling anyone
Lift neighbouring manhole covers to let more sewage escape
new.explanation: An overflow exposes people to raw sewage and can reach a watercourse. The first priorities are to keep people away, report it and begin the facility's spill response steps. Sending sewage to a storm drain moves the pollution into a receiving water.

new.question: What is the main purpose of cleaning gravity sewers on a regular schedule?
options: To remove grease, grit and roots that reduce capacity and cause blockages and overflows
To raise the hydrogen sulfide concentration in the sewage
To increase the groundwater infiltration rate
To make the pipe walls rougher for better flow
new.explanation: Grease, grit and roots build up in sewers and cut the flow area. Routine cleaning keeps the pipe at its design capacity and prevents blockages and backups.

new.question: Which observation most strongly points to inflow, rather than infiltration, as the main source of extra flow in a sanitary sewer?
options: Flow stays high for weeks after the rain stops and drops slowly
Flow is highest at night when little wastewater is produced and does not change with rain
Flow is unchanged during and after storms
Flow rises sharply during a storm and falls back to normal within hours after it ends
new.explanation: Inflow enters directly through sources such as cross-connected roof drains or manhole covers, so it appears quickly with rainfall and ends quickly. Infiltration through cracks and joints rises and falls more slowly with the groundwater level.

new.question: Why should an operator not rely on smell to tell whether hydrogen sulfide is present in a manhole?
options: Hydrogen sulfide has no odour at any concentration, so smell cannot be used at all
The gas gives off a smell only when it has first been mixed with methane in the space
At higher concentrations it dulls the sense of smell, so the odour can disappear while the gas is still present
Only specially trained workers are physically able to smell the gas at any level
new.explanation: Hydrogen sulfide smells like rotten eggs at low concentrations, but at higher levels it paralyses the sense of smell. A lack of odour is not a sign that the space is safe, so a gas monitor must be used.

new.question: Why should a hydrant valve be closed slowly after use?
options: Closing quickly lets air enter the main and lowers the chlorine residual
A sudden stop in the flowing water causes a pressure surge (water hammer) that can damage pipes and fittings
Slow closing keeps the hydrant drained for winter
Fast closing makes the hydrant leak at the barrel
new.explanation: Flowing water has momentum. When a valve closes quickly the water is stopped suddenly and the pressure spikes along the main. Closing slowly lets the velocity fall gradually.

new.question: What is the purpose of a check valve on the discharge line of a lift station pump?
options: To prevent flow from returning from the force main into the pump when it stops
To raise the discharge pressure of the pump while it is running at full speed
To let air escape from the wet well when the water level rises quickly
To measure the flow rate leaving the station and send it to the control room
new.explanation: When a pump stops, the liquid in the force main would flow back toward the wet well. The check valve closes and keeps it in the line, which also protects the idle pump from spinning backward.

new.question: Which condition in a sewer force main most often leads to the formation of hydrogen sulfide?
options: Fast flow with a high dissolved oxygen concentration
A low sewage temperature with frequent mixing
A short pipe with continuous aeration
Long detention times that let the sewage turn anaerobic
new.explanation: When sewage sits in a full pipe for a long time the dissolved oxygen is used up. Bacteria then reduce sulfate to hydrogen sulfide, which is released at discharge points and causes odour, corrosion and safety hazards.

new.question: What does the term chlorine demand mean?
options: The chlorine left in the water after disinfection
The amount of chlorine used up by reactions with substances in the water
The amount of chlorine stored in the cylinder
The dose needed to raise the pH to 7
new.explanation: Chlorine demand is the dose added minus the residual that remains. It is consumed by organic matter, iron, manganese, ammonia and other substances in the water.

new.question: Which list shows the steps of conventional surface water treatment in the usual order?
options: Coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, filtration, disinfection
Filtration, sedimentation, coagulation, flocculation, disinfection
Disinfection, coagulation, filtration, flocculation, sedimentation
Sedimentation, coagulation, disinfection, filtration, flocculation
new.explanation: Coagulant is mixed in first, flocculation grows the floc, sedimentation settles it, filtration removes what is left and disinfection is the final barrier.

new.question: What is the purpose of backwashing a rapid gravity filter?
options: To add a chlorine dose directly into the filter media before the water is filtered
To raise the turbidity of the filtered water so that it matches the raw water
To change the grain size of the sand each time the filter is put back in service
To remove the solids trapped in the media so the filter can run again at its normal capacity
new.explanation: As a filter runs, particles fill the spaces in the media and head loss rises. Reversing the flow lifts and cleans the bed and washes the solids to waste.

new.question: What is a day tank used for in a chemical feed system?
options: To store the plant's entire bulk chemical supply
To neutralize spilled chemical
To hold a small working supply of chemical near the feed pump
To mix two incompatible chemicals together
new.explanation: A day tank holds about a day's use of chemical close to the feed pump. It limits the amount at hand and lets the operator check the feed rate by watching the level drop.

new.question: What does a high sludge volume index (SVI) in an activated sludge plant indicate?
options: The sludge settles and compacts very well
The sludge settles poorly, as in bulking
The sludge has no filamentous bacteria
The plant has too little mixed liquor
new.explanation: SVI is the volume in mL occupied by one gram of settled sludge. A high value means the floc is light and settles slowly, which risks solids carrying over the clarifier weir.

new.question: What is the purpose of the anoxic zone in a biological nutrient removal process?
options: To convert nitrate to nitrogen gas using the organic matter in the wastewater
To add dissolved oxygen so that ammonia can be converted to nitrate by bacteria
To settle the sludge out of the mixed liquor before it is returned to the tank
To disinfect the effluent with chlorine before it is discharged to the river
new.explanation: In the anoxic zone there is no free dissolved oxygen, so bacteria use nitrate as the oxygen source and release nitrogen gas. This is denitrification and it removes nitrogen from the water.

new.question: Why is post-aeration often used before effluent is discharged?
options: To lower the effluent temperature so that it is the same as the receiving water
To add more ammonia to the effluent so that the fish have more food to eat
To remove all of the remaining solids before the effluent reaches the outfall
To raise the dissolved oxygen in the effluent to protect life in the receiving water
new.explanation: Treated effluent can leave with low dissolved oxygen, especially after disinfection or denitrification. Aerating it before release helps keep the receiving water able to support fish.

new.question: What does a composite effluent sample show that a single grab sample does not?
options: The quality at one instant only
The temperature of the sludge
The average quality over a period of time
The flow rate at the weir
new.explanation: A composite is made from many small portions taken over time or in proportion to flow. It represents the average conditions, while a grab sample shows only the moment it was taken.

options: 20.8 mg·min/L
30 mg·min/L
26.2 mg·min/L
3.0 mg·min/L
new.explanation: CT is the disinfectant residual multiplied by the effective contact time. 1.2 mg/L × 25 min = 30 mg·min/L.

options: 160 kg/d
16 kg/d
80 kg/d
new.explanation: One mg/L applied to one ML/d is one kg/d. So 20 mg/L × 8 ML/d = 160 kg/d.

new.question: Why is a free chlorine residual kept in a distribution system?
options: To make the water look clearer in the pipes and at the tap
To raise the pH of the water as it moves through the system
To remove the hardness from the water before it reaches customers
To keep protecting the water from microbial growth and contamination after it leaves the plant
new.explanation: A residual that remains in the pipes keeps disinfecting as the water travels, and it gives a warning if contamination enters. Without it, bacteria can regrow in the system.

new.question: What is the idea behind the multi-barrier approach to drinking water safety?
options: One strong disinfection step is enough, so the other safeguards can be skipped
Water is treated only when the source has been found to be badly polluted
Several independent safeguards are used, so one failing does not lead to unsafe water
Testing at the tap replaces the need for treatment at the plant
new.explanation: The barriers include source protection, treatment, a protected distribution system and monitoring. Each layer backs up the others.

new.question: What does the UV transmittance (UVT) of a water sample measure?
options: The number of UV lamps that are lit
The share of UV light that passes through the water
The chlorine demand of the water
The pH of the water
new.explanation: UVT is the fraction of UV light that gets through the water over a set path length. Lower UVT means more light is absorbed, so less reaches the organisms and the UV dose falls.

new.question: What is the purpose of a standard operating procedure (SOP) in a treatment plant?
options: To set out the steps of a task so that it is done the same way each time
To replace operator training completely
To let each operator choose a different method
To record the daily weather
new.explanation: An SOP documents how a task should be done safely and correctly. It helps staff on different shifts get the same result and gives new operators a reference.

options: A single check valve
A double check valve assembly
An air gap
A pressure vacuum breaker
new.explanation: An air gap is a physical open space between the supply outlet and the possible source of contamination. Nothing can flow back across it, unlike mechanical devices that can foul or fail.

new.question: What is an easement?
options: A pipe fitting that joins two water mains of different diameters together
A legal right to use a part of someone else's land for a specific purpose, such as a buried pipe
A permit that allows a utility to discharge treated water to a river
A type of valve that is installed on large transmission mains
new.explanation: Utilities often need to place pipes across private land. An easement gives that right without transferring ownership of the land.

options: A real or possible link between a drinking water system and a source of contamination
A valve that joins two water mains of the same quality
A pipe that carries water from a well to a plant
A meter installed at a customer's service
new.explanation: A cross-connection lets contaminants enter the potable system if the pressure drops or flow reverses. Backflow prevention devices are used to protect against it.

options: To avoid having to test for the chlorine residual anywhere in the system
Because the plant outlet is never allowed to be sampled by the operators
To reduce the total number of tests that the laboratory must carry out
To show the quality of the water at different points that customers receive it
new.explanation: Water quality can change as it travels through pipes, storage and dead ends. Sampling around the system shows what customers actually get.

options: A 99.9 percent reduction in the number of organisms present
A 90 percent reduction in the number of organisms present
A 99.99 percent reduction in the number of organisms
A 99.999 percent reduction in the number of organisms present

Contact information, assigned roles and the steps to follow during an emergency
Only the chemical supplier's price list and the delivery schedule for the year
Only a list of the customer complaints that were received in the past year

new.question: Why must a sample for bacteriological testing be kept cool and delivered to the laboratory promptly?
options: The sample would change colour and make the test result harder to read
The glass container would crack if the sample were allowed to warm up
The chlorine residual in the sample would increase while it was kept warm
Organisms in the sample can die or multiply, which would change the result

Lead pipes remove minerals from the water
Lead can dissolve into water that stands in contact with the pipe
Lead reacts with the chlorine to form gas

new.question: What is added to a sample bottle for bacteriological analysis of chlorinated water, and why?
options: Sodium hydroxide, to raise the pH of the sample so bacteria survive longer
Sodium thiosulfate, to neutralize the chlorine so it stops killing bacteria in the bottle
Alum, to settle the particles out of the sample before it is tested
Extra chlorine, to preserve the sample until it reaches the laboratory

20 percent
0.5 percent
